_policy: Quarantined stories still RUN and are still REPORTED, but their failures do
not turn the storybook-probe job red. Quarantine is a stopgap for a story
whose flakiness is understood but not yet fixed — never a parking lot.
Rules enforced by scripts/probe-stories.mjs, which refuses to run if broken:
- at most `maxEntries` stories may be quarantined at once;
- every entry needs `id`, `reason` and an ISO `expires` date;
- on and after `expires` the entry stops shielding the story, so the job
goes red again and someone has to fix, delete or consciously renew it.
A quarantined story that passes is reported as READY so it can be removed.
`a11yEntries` does the same for ONE axe rule on one story (`id` "*" means
every story): the violation is still printed, it just does not gate. Same
cap (`maxA11yEntries`), same required reason and expiry. Only `critical`
and `serious` violations gate in the first place — lowering that threshold
instead of quarantining a rule is not an option, because it silences every

entries.reason: The app calls preventDefault() on every Tab keydown (machines/actors/keyboardActor.ts), so Tab is sent to tmux and the page has no keyboard tab order at all — not in the header, the tab strip or the sidebar. Verified with a real browser Tab, not only with userEvent. The check is correct and stays; freeing Tab while the chrome (rather than a pane) holds the keyboard is the fix, and is not a story-side change.

Mermaid loads each diagram type as a DYNAMIC import, and Vite's dep optimizer only discovers `flowDiagram-*` when a story first renders one — it then re-optimizes, renames the chunk, and the already-loaded mermaid entry still points at the old name. Observed in a real browser: the page requests flowDiagram-HODETNUW-OY4LGNFO.js, the file on disk is flowDiagram-HODETNUW-ZXSBNWFE.js, and the server answers 504 Outdated Optimize Dep, so mermaid rejects and MermaidBlock renders the error instead of an SVG. Neither optimizeDeps.include (covers mermaid's ENTRY, not the diagram modules) nor exclude (the story then never mounts at all — strictly worse) fixes it; both were tried and reverted. The same re-optimization reload is what tore down the probe's contexts and left storybook-probe sitting until its 30-minute timeout in CI. The fix is a Storybook/Vite dep-handling change for mermaid, not a story change.

Exceeds every budget the probe has — still `probe-timeout` at a 200s per-story deadline, locally and on CI. What it is NOT, each ruled out by measurement rather than reasoning: not the `useFloatingSurface` render loop fixed in 1832264 (this survives it, and the page's main thread answers an outside eval, so nothing is spinning); not the a11y scan (the axe deadline added in f5ad22b reports a NOTE, and none fires); not a concurrency artefact (it fails alone at PROBE_CONCURRENCY=1); and not an unbounded wait in the story, whose every waitFor is 5-8s and whose waitForTree is 8s. Observed detail worth keeping: opening the story directly leaves the sidebar tree unrendered (0 treeitems, 0 menuitems), so the right-click the story is about never gets a row to aim at. Cause not yet identified — quarantined to keep the job honest rather than because it is understood.

a11yEntries.reason: A pane header carries role=tablist but its tabs are spans without role=tab (components/PaneHeader.tsx). The roles have to be finished off together with aria-required-parent; neither is a story-side fix.
The other half of the same defect: .tab-name carries role=tab with no tablist ancestor (components/WindowTabs.tsx).
Inactive tab titles, pane titles and the status-line hints are drawn at the theme's inactive opacity and fall under 4.5:1. Fixing it is a theme-palette decision, not a test change.
The selectable terminal content sits inside an aria-hidden subtree while still being focusable (components/TerminalPane). Needs the pane's aria model reworked.
The pane-tab strip (.pane-tabs) scrolls but takes no keyboard focus; it needs a tabindex and arrow-key handling in components/PaneHeader.tsx.
A tab-overview slot is a button containing its own close button (components/TabOverview.tsx); the outer control has to stop being a button.
The tab-overview grid takes an ARIA input role with no accessible name (components/TabOverview.tsx).
